newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-UNRATED COLON THRASH RIVER 5-1 TO STAY TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNRATED COLON THRASH RIVER 5-1 TO STAY TOP.

text.p: Unrated Colon, who began the Argentine championship with the sole aim of avoiding relegation, thrashed pre-tournament favourites River Plate 5-1 on Sunday to stay top of the table.

Colon were 4-1 ahead by halftime, added a fifth early in the second half and could have recorded an even bigger win but for the heroics of River goalkeeper Roberto Bonano and their own poor finishing.
Uruguayan Marcelo Saralegui scored a first-half hat-trick for Colon with Cristian Castillo scoring the other two.

The result kept unbeaten Colon, who have never won a major title, one point ahead of Newell's Old Boys, who won 2-1 away to Gimnasia-Jujuy, in the Clausura championship, the second of two competitions held in the Argentine season.
The defeat completed a miserable week for River, champions of the Apertura championship held earlier in the season.
River lost 4-1 at home to Estudiantes last weekend and in mid-week were knocked out of the South American Libertadores Cup, which they won last year, by local rivals Racing Club.
The team appear to have lost their way completely after selling top player Ariel Ortega to Spanish club Valencia and, almost inevitably, speculation is mounting about the future of coach Ramon Diaz.
River trail Colon by seven points, although they have played one game less.
Boca Juniors, the country's most popular club, ended a miserable run in style by beating Gimnasia-La Plata 6-1, Uruguay's Sergio Martinez scoring four of the goals.

They avenged a 6-0 drubbing at home to the same team last year, on the day they reinaugurated a revamped La Bonbonera stadium, but the win came too late to revive their championship hopes and they are still stuck in mid-table.
Velez Sarsfield recovered from Thursday's shock, when they were dumped out of the Libertadores after losing at home to Peruvians Sporting Cristal by winning 1-0 at Rosario Central.
